priorStatuses.title: Remove the message listener during cleanup

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body: After any caller invokes the disposer while the socket remains alive, the handler stays retained and continues receiving messages. Repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners, memory, and duplicate side effects.

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the interval in the polling disposer
findings.body: Invoking the returned cleanup no longer stops polling. The callback and captured state remain live indefinitely, refresh work continues after teardown, and in Node.js the referenced interval can prevent process shutdown.

findings.title: [P1] Remove the message listener during cleanup
findings.body: This previously reported defect remains open after current-source revalidation. Evidence: Current src/socket.ts line 3 still returns a no-op disposer immediately after registering handler with socket.on; the full diff shows this PR removed the prior socket.off("message", handler) call. Cleanup therefore cannot detach the listener, so disposed consumers remain invoked and repeated cycles retain handlers.
